sentiment_score_definition: x <= -0.35: Bearish; -0.35 < x <= -0.15: Somewhat-Bearish; -0.15 < x < 0.15: Neutral; 0.15 <= x < 0.35: Somewhat_Bullish; x >= 0.35: Bullish
relevance_score_definition: 0 < x <= 1, with a higher score indicating higher relevance.

feed.title: These Stocks Moved the Most Today: Super Micro, Alphabet, AMD, Lilly, Reddit, AbbVie, Qorvo, Garmin, and More
feed.summary: Stocks experienced a downturn on Wednesday, despite Alphabet's earnings surpassing expectations. Investors are now anticipating upcoming reports from Microsoft and Meta Platforms. The U.S. gross domestic product for the third quarter also came in lower than predicted, though the economy continues to show solid growth.

feed.title: Palmetto Grain Brokerage - Previous Tech Stock Strength Lifts the Broader Market
feed.summary: The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrials saw gains, primarily driven by strong tech stock performance and better-than-expected US economic data, including Q3 personal consumption and ADP employment figures. However, the Nasdaq 100 experienced pressure from negative corporate news concerning Super Micro Computer and Advanced Micro Devices. The article also touches on fluctuating interest rates, key upcoming economic reports, and earnings season updates.

feed.title: If You Had Invested $1000 into American Express When Warren Buffett First Invested in 1991, Here's How Much You'd Have Now
feed.summary: This article illustrates the significant returns an investor would have received by mirroring Warren Buffett's 1991 investment in American Express. A hypothetical $1,000 investment made when Buffett first invested would now be worth approximately $81,040, demonstrating the power of long-term value investing. The piece also recounts Buffett's history with American Express, including his initial investment during the "Salad Oil Scandal" and his continued confidence in the company despite economic challenges.
